concept: A two-person stage piece where the questioner utters ONLY questions, never a statement, and the audience watches a confident belief visibly collapse in real time.
A live 'autopsy' theatre: a volunteer's stated belief is laid on a table and dissected, each question removing a layer until what's left is examined under a lamp.
A Jenga tower whose blocks are labeled with the premises of a belief; each unanswerable question pulls a block until the whole thing falls.
An app that NEVER answers and only asks, interrogating the user's own typed opinion until they revise it themselves.
An escape room whose only exit is to abandon a false assumption the room keeps questioning you about.
A mock courtroom cross-examining an everyday belief ('money buys happiness') with no witnesses — only questions.
Improv comedy where one player may only ask questions and must still 'win' the scene.
An animation rendering each Socratic question as a brick pulled from a building, until the edifice of a belief stands on nothing.
The method as a GPS that only ever says 'are you sure?' and reroutes you off every confident road.
A real Socratic dialogue printed with each question color-coded by function (define, counterexample, expose contradiction) so you SEE the gears.
A 'Socratic rubber duck' desk toy that, when you explain your idea to it, asks one devastating question back.
Staged as literal midwifery (Socrates' maieutics): the questioner 'delivers' the idea the respondent didn't know they were carrying.
Two actors — one holds a belief, one only questions; performed twice, the second time the audience supplies the questions.
A board game where you advance only by asking a question your opponent cannot answer about their own claim.
Audience members 'sing' a confident opinion and the host interrupts each line with a question.
A well-illustrated lecture on Socrates' life, trial, and the historical method.
A handout of 20 Socratic questioning prompts for teachers.
A formal two-sided debate on a proposition.
A poster walking through 'why?' five times on a sample claim.
A podcast where the host Socratically interviews a guest about a belief they hold dear, never asserting.
AR glasses that overlay a probing question on any confident statement you hear.
Film a six-year-old relentlessly asking 'but why?' to an expert until the expert hits bedrock.
A staged session where a 'therapist' only questions a client's catastrophic belief until it dissolves.
The audience votes on a claim, a questioner asks questions live, then they re-vote — watching the room change its own mind.
Two AIs — one asserts a belief, the other only questions — livestreamed until the first concedes.
A cooking-show where each 'ingredient' is a premise the chef questions until the recipe collapses.
A physical maze where each turn poses a question about your assumption; the wrong assumption is a dead end.
Take a viral hot-take live on stage and dismantle it with questions in front of its author.
A puppet Socrates questions a puppet sophist whose strings visibly tangle as he contradicts himself.
A comic where each panel is one question and the speech bubbles shrink as the respondent's certainty does.
A 'reverse TED talk': no claims, just 18 minutes of questions put to the audience.
An onion peeled on stage, each layer a labeled assumption removed by a question, until nothing is at the center.
A phone hotline you call with a certainty; the operator only asks questions back.
Students in a fishbowl: the outer ring may only ask questions, the inner must defend a claim.
A 'market' where confidence in a claim is a stock price that drops live with each unanswered question.
A fencing-style duel where touches land only via a question that exposes a contradiction.
Live-edit a confident claim where an editor may only add '[why?]' tags until the article unravels.
Audience anonymously submits strongly-held beliefs; a host questions a random one live until it collapses.
A sung dialogue where questions are the melody and the answers keep changing key until atonal.
A single actor argues with their reflection, the reflection only ever asking questions, exposing self-deception.
Ask 'what would break if that were true?' to expose hidden assumptions.
Present two contradictory expert quotes and ask which reasoning is stronger.
